findings.title: canManage() grants manage on groups based on VIEW scope
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() falls back to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). An admin who only holds the VIEW scope on all groups is therefore treated as able to manage groups. requireManage() is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, so this lets a view-only admin create top-level groups. The fallback should check only MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission passes the resource id where hasPermission expects a group id
findings.body: Inside the findByType callback, hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) is called, and the id is added to the granted set. hasPermission looks the resource up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). In V2 the resource name is the group id, not the resource UUID, so the lookup finds nothing. It then falls back to the all-groups type resource. The set returned also contains resource UUIDs instead of group ids, which breaks the user-search group filter. The code should use groupResource.getName() for both the permission check and the returned set. The test only passes by accident, since a resource id may equal the group id in some stores.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Groups type resource is missing
findings.body: getResourceTypeResource can return null, for example if the realm was created before the Groups type existed. policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) is then called with null and resource.getScopes() would also fail, so the permission check throws instead of returning false. There is no null check, unlike the null-safe handling elsewhere. Existing realms with admin permissions enabled will not have a Groups resource, because AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early when the client already exists.

findings.title: Group view lookup no longer guarded by canView()
findings.body: The `!auth.users().canView()` guard was removed. getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() performs the same check internally for the regular admin-role case. It returns an empty set only if users().canView() is true, so the behaviour is the same for that case. However, session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...) is now set even when the caller can view all users, because the V2 canView depends on hasPermission. When it is set, grantIfNoPermission(true) is also invoked, which widens the grant. This is subtle and needs review and tests.
